findings.title: `include_website_name` lacks `?`, so `website_name` is always serialized and bypasses TL0 hiding
findings.body:
ActiveModel::Serializers only looks for `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` has no trailing `?`, so it is never called and `website_name` is serialized for every user.

The raw `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is hidden for TL0 users seen by anonymous visitors (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). `website_name` is not in that list and has no working filter. Anonymous visitors therefore receive the website host, and now also its path, for TL0 users. This defeats the spam-mitigation intent of hiding untrusted fields.

In the template, `{{#if model.website_name}}` will also render a globe and a link with an empty href for these users.

Fix: add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, or define `include_website_name?` with the same restriction check.

findings.title: Untrusted-attributes spec doesn't cover new `website_name` field
findings.body: The TL0/anonymous spec still checks only the old untrusted attribute list. Because `website_name` is missing from it, the spec does not catch that `website_name` is exposed to anonymous visitors for TL0 users. Add `website_name` to the list.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated domains under public suffixes as the same site
findings.body: The same-length branch compares everything after the first label. A forum at `forum.co.uk` would treat any `anything.co.uk` website as the same site. A forum at `forum.github.io` would do the same for any `x.github.io`. In those cases the full URL path of an unrelated external site is shown as if it were on the instance's own domain. Comparing registrable domains (public-suffix aware) would avoid this.
